note: Attacker-controlled bytes after the two-byte fuzzer prefix become the JSON text that drives parsing and later serialization.
The controlled JSON is parsed into a flexbuffer/flatbuffer object graph that can later be rendered back to text.

The implementation assumes vector-like references are safe to stringify, but the underlying vector contents can include malformed string/blob references that violate the bounds needed by EscapeString.
Vector elements are forwarded to the generic stringification helper, preserving the attacker-controlled element data into the sink path.
Stringifying a blob uses blob.size() as the read bound for EscapeString; a malformed blob reference can make this read past the allocated buffer and trigger the heap-buffer-overflow.
